verdict.rationale: Kushki markets a JS library that relies on Kushki's own PCI compliance ('Máxima seguridad con PCI de Kushki'), plus a hosted payment button that redirects payments to a secure portal. Its docs list 'Direct charge (without token)' as a separate path, which implies tokenized charging is the standard flow. The evidence consists only of page titles, though; nothing explicitly states that raw card data never reaches merchant servers or that merchants qualify for reduced PCI scope (e.g., SAQ A). Missing for 10: explicit documentation of client-side tokenization keeping PAN off merchant servers, a stated PCI scope-reduction or SAQ level, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can keep my systems out of most of PCI DSS scope because card data is tokenized and never touches my servers
